name: TA2552
keyCapabilities: Phishing for O365 third-party application access
Malicious application development for cloud service access
Infrastructure concealment via Cloudflare and compromised sites
Credential harvesting through scoped permissions (Mail.Read, Contacts.Read)
recommendedActions: Audit O365/Google Workspace third-party application permissions to identify and revoke high-risk or unnecessary grants.
Configure alert rules for non-standard or suspicious OAuth scopes like Mail.Read and Contacts.Read.
Implement detection rules for redirects from known phishing URLs to Microsoft's consent page.
Block known malicious domains including those on the .xyz, .in, and .ru TLDs associated with MexOAuth.
Conduct security awareness training specifically highlighting OAuth 'consent' scams and brand-mimicking lures.
Monitor for discrepancies between landing page content (e.g., Netflix) and subsequent redirect outcomes.
Restrict end-users from registering third-party apps if not required by business operations.
Use CASB or identity protection tools to alert on access requests from unusual IP ranges or geographic locations.
campaignsText: The actor is primarily associated with the 'MexOAuth' campaign, which since early 2020 has targeted Spanish-speaking users, specifically in Mexico. This campaign utilizes a sophisticated infrastructure of custom domains and compromised sites to host OAuth consent pages. They frequently employ lures related to local government services or popular streaming memberships to drive user interaction. Their operations are characterized by high precision in choosing target languages and regional themes to maximize conversion rates for token theft.
description: TA2552 is a sophisticated threat actor that specializes in abusing Microsoft Office 365 third-party application (3PA) access via OAuth token phishing. The group targets Spanish-speaking individuals, particularly in Mexico, utilizing high-affinity brand lures to gain unauthorized permissions to sensitive email and contact data.
goals: The primary goal of TA2552 is the theft of sensitive information and long-term account persistence through OAuth token harvesting. By acquiring 'read-only' permissions, they can conduct sophisticated reconnaissance on target mailboxes and contacts to identify high-value targets or intercept communications between financial institutions. Their targeting strategy specifically leverages language-specific lures (Spanish) to engage users in Mexico, though their broader intelligence profile indicates interests in the government, defense, and energy sectors across several countries.
